sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Parth has a real electrical-equipment business, a credible technical niche and a disclosed ₹471 crore executable order book. New GIS and eastern-India capacity could expand its addressable product and customer base. However, nonexclusive licences and concentrated customers limit the moat; two years of poor cash realization and material bank-return/proceeds inconsistencies prevent ordinary return underwriting.

At ₹530.05 on 19 October 2026, current-share market value is ₹740.37 crore, or 52.00 times FY26 reported PAT. The stipulated, funded base case returns about 12.01% annually versus a 15% hurdle, before resolving the reliability questions. This is a conditional model, not an actionable target. The appropriate research priority is to establish cash availability and reconcile bank submissions, then verify that new orders convert into collected profit and attractive incremental returns. It is not a demonstrated compounder or an underwritten 5× opportunity at this price.

The exact issuer is Parth Electricals & Engineering Limited, NSE PARTH, SM/Emerge, ISIN INE1H7V01011, CIN L32202GJ2007PLC050751. Its pre-listing CIN began with U rather than L. The financial scope is standalone Indian AS under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules 2021, not IndAS. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026; market reference is 19 October because 20 October was an exchange holiday. Financial balances are anchored to 31 March 2026. June monitoring, released in August, and the actual July allotment update the funding bridge without pretending that projected October cash is observed. Investment horizon is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, actual days/365.25, with a 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle and 12%/18% sensitivity. ₹500,000 is an illustrative liquidity reference, not a disclosed user holding.

At the reference price, two lots are 800 shares costing ₹424,040, while three lots are 1,200 shares costing ₹636,060. One lot costs ₹212,020. sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Diagnostic BQS is 4.92, displayed 4.9/10. Raw GQS is 5.70, capped at 5.0 because persistent weak cash realization triggers the framework override. IAS is NS: weighted coverage is 65% and its mathematical bounds are 3.18–6.33. Those bounds are not a confidence interval or a ranked point score. R is missing rather than imputed to 5. Other factors retain evidence-supported diagnostic scores. IAS uses unrounded BQS and exact Decimal contributions; display rounding is HALF_UP.

REV uses all six available annual observations and the five-year period, not the flattering FY22 trough. CAP uses a multi-year organic capital bridge rather than the latest ROCE alone. CASH 2 reflects both weak FY25/FY26 realization and the four-year conversion deficit, not merely one delayed shipment. GOV 4 does not trigger the governance ≤3 override, and no fraud finding is invented. The separate G2 Hold nevertheless governs the final classification. Score sensitivity varies CAP and CASH by one point without falsely turning a diagnostic number into an investable rank.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Parth designs, assembles/manufactures and sells ring main units (RMUs), compact and prefabricated substations, medium/low-voltage panels, electrical houses and related equipment. It also supplies installation, testing, commissioning, cable-accessory and EPC services. Buyers include utilities, EPC contractors and industrial customers. Procurement includes licensed components, fabricated assemblies and metal-intensive equipment. Order, manufacture, inspection, dispatch, site acceptance and payment are distinct milestones; a new order does not release working capital.

FY26 manufacturing sales were ₹170.3623 crore versus ₹166.0798 crore, only 2.58% growth, while services increased to ₹27.6228 crore from ₹8.5586 crore. These audited categories differ from the presentation’s product/EPC grouping, so no artificial product bridge is forced between them. Audited FOB exports were ₹31.0269 crore versus nil in FY25; exports also existed in FY23/FY24, and foreign receivables are not a substitute export-sales measure.

No acquisition revenue is identified. A promoter-linked US business can assist customer access but is not a listed-company subsidiary or proof that all overseas demand is unrelated. Qualification, manufacturing throughput and field support form the operating proposition. Working-capital discipline and repeat commissioning capacity determine whether that proposition creates shareholder value.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The strongest moat candidate is a local qualification-and-service capability: type-tested designs, utility/customer approvals, integration discipline and field engineering create switching friction. FY25 RMU output was 2,308 units against 2,460 capacity, or 93.82%; panels were 916 against 985. These are observable operations, not merely a future-market story. Stocking smaller RMUs can shorten delivery, though the service advantage itself requires inventory capital.

The countercase is explicit. Schneider and Hezong licences are nonexclusive, territory-limited and terminable; competitors can access similar technology. The licensor can also be an important supplier. Larger equipment groups and domestic RMU/panel manufacturers compete with Parth, but they are not a sufficiently matched valuation peer set to justify importing their multiples.

FY25 top-ten customers represented 86.46% of sales and the top five 67.49%; no long-term customer agreements were identified in the prospectus. Industrial orders generally lack raw-material price escalation; certain EPC cables/transformers are exceptions. The company has not demonstrated broad pricing power or proprietary global IP. MOAT 5 recognizes real qualification and service friction without confusing customer names, licences or high utilization with an exclusive franchise.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
FY21–FY26 revenue rose from ₹68.346512 crore to ₹198.0044 crore, a preferred five-year CAGR of approximately 23.70% based on six observations. FY23–FY26 growth was much faster, about 44.57%, while the FY22 trough produces an even higher four-year rate. Neither shorter measure replaces the available five-year history. FY22 revenue of ₹37.99 crore and a ₹1.54 crore loss show the observed business was not steadily compounding; the cause is not guessed where the source evidence is insufficient.

FY25 added ₹87.8868 crore of revenue, versus ₹23.3327 crore in FY26. FY26 H1 revenue ₹80.3993 crore compared with derived FY25 H1 ₹69.90 crore means 15.02% growth. H2 revenue ₹117.6051 crore compared with ₹104.7717 crore means 12.25%. Both comparable halves justify the maximum net −1 trajectory adjustment to the 20–30% CAGR anchor of 8, yielding REV 7. Future backlog does not earn an offsetting growth point before execution.

No acquisition perimeter change is identified, but unit/pricing data are insufficient to call all growth volume-led. Increased manufacturing capacity, services/EPC mix, exports and project timing are plausible contributors. The delayed ₹25 crore export-shipment explanation cannot simply be added to audited revenue. October backlog of ₹471 crore is 2.38 times FY26 sales, an opportunity subject to capacity, acceptance, cancellations, margins and collection, not guaranteed one-year income.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The runway has concrete elements: RMU orders can use existing capacity; GIS broadens the product range; Khordha/Odisha can improve eastern customer access; export qualification and field services may diversify demand. Yet order book is not cash or unconditional collectible profit. Inspection slots, components, subcontracting, guarantees and customer acceptance can bottleneck conversion even if demand is strong.

Capital precedes collection. March PPE, intangibles and CWIP totaled ₹40.573 crore, with inventory ₹41.602 crore. June monitoring confirmed another ₹3.85 crore of GIS expenditure, but Odisha object spending remained zero and both projects carried three-month implementation delays. Management subsequently favored leased Odisha premises and an October operating target. The October order filing refers to the new Khordha facility but does not independently establish full commissioned capacity or returns.

Remaining project commitments overlap remaining IPO object budgets; they must not be added twice. The model ring-fences eligible proceeds, reserves actual remaining project cash costs and continues maintenance and growth capex after the initial budget ends. Raw GQS 5.70 is capped at 5.0 because persistent poor cash realization weakens the quality of growth. Collected earnings and attractive returns from new assets could improve the case; repeated equity funding of inventory and receivables could instead enlarge sales while diluting owners.

incremental_capital.interpretation: Standalone organic capital bridge supports a cautious CAP score, not a project-cohort estimate. Excluding all cash overstates efficiency if deposits support operations; including IPO cash understates efficiency before project deployment. Gratuity catch-up and product/EPC mix shift further limit precision.

operating_cross_check.scope: Basic operating NWC is inventory plus total trade receivables less trade payables and customer advances. This subset excludes other operating advances, government/tax assets and provisions; the residual is not falsely assigned to a single cause. Full treatment is bounded by cash-included/excluded capital proxies. No acquisition capital is identified.
operating_cross_check.interpretation: Cash capex less depreciation nearly matches productive asset growth. The remaining financing-to-operating residual requires other assets/liabilities, noncash accruals and comparative reclassifications; insufficient granular comparable inputs prevent a fully allocated reconciliation. It is a disclosed scope residual, not evidence of missing cash.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Management has technical operating experience and substantial ownership. These are alignment indicators, not proof that every allocation protects minority holders. FY26 related purchases were ₹2.9117 crore, related sales ₹0.2050 crore, director-asset purchases ₹0.38 crore and enterprise balances ₹0.4456 crore. Transactions are disclosed and reported compliant. Promoter-linked US flows nevertheless deserve separate arm’s-length and collection checks rather than being counted twice as independent export demand.

The full audit record matters. FY25’s clean headline opinion coexisted with an unrecognized ₹1.27 crore gratuity liability and audit-trail operation only from 24 February 2025. FY24 also lacked the required trail. FY26 reports ₹1.40 crore booked and full-year trail operation, positive remediation that must be credited. The historical issue is not carried as a duplicate unbooked liability after FY26.

Other questions remain open. December 2025 bank returns differ materially from the books, and CARO itself disagrees with Note 35’s book amount. Generic stock/receivable adjustments are not an itemized reconciliation. CARO’s idle-IPO-deposit figure conflicts with the audited-result note and monitoring reports. No fraud, default or rating non-cooperation is established by these findings.

Execution is mixed. High prior capacity utilization and actual GIS spending show delivery, but the original FY26 project timetable was missed. May’s inventory-clearance and September/October commissioning targets lack independently verified complete closure by cutoff. January’s clarification supplied an omitted certificate and corrected the MD designation; May’s refile improved searchability. Neither reconciled bank returns. GOV 4 and EXEC 5 reflect that balance, with G2 Hold carrying the material consequence.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Cash is the central operating weakness. FY26 CFO was −₹4.0617 crore against PAT ₹14.2379 crore, following FY25 CFO ₹0.3019 crore against PAT ₹10.1169 crore. Four-year FY23–FY26 CFO was ₹6.8746 crore against PAT ₹31.4127 crore: only 21.88% conversion. Capex over those years totaled ₹40.1684 crore. Inventory growth absorbed ₹26.8723 crore and total receivables ₹8.3721 crore in FY26; higher payables funded ₹20.1210 crore and customer advances also increased. Stocks and receivables are not automatically losses, but they are not cash profits.

Core EBITDA equals PBT plus finance cost and depreciation minus other income. FY26 core EBITDA was ₹20.8481 crore versus ₹17.5327 crore, 18.91% growth, below PAT growth of about 40.74%. Finance cost fell ₹1.524 crore and other income rose ₹1.413 crore, much of it interest. FY25 gratuity underprovision complicates the comparison. The exact FY26 historical catch-up versus recurring service-cost split is not isolated; a possible 0–₹1.27 crore pretax addback is a sensitivity, not a permanent margin entitlement.

The organic capital bridge normalizes tax at 25.17% and uses core EBIT. It compares FY23–FY26 incremental NOPAT with equity plus debt minus all cash and policy investments, then provides an all-cash-included denominator. The resulting return bracket is around 10–16%, tested against 11/13/15% capital costs. New CWIP and late commissioning depress near-term returns but do not prove future high returns. No acquired earnings are mixed into the numerator.

Some apparent discrepancies are classification changes. FY26 ageing ₹39.2426 crore includes long-term receivables; FY25 prospectus and later comparative have the same ₹30.8704 crore total despite different current/long-term splits. The ₹0.0029 crore cash-flow endpoint residual is small and separately retained. In contrast, recurring bank-return differences and idle-proceeds inconsistencies remain material. December’s stated ₹12.3609 crore difference is roughly 86.82% of FY26 PAT; March’s −₹1.9246 crore is roughly 13.52%. Note 35’s ₹34.8415 crore book amount versus bank ₹47.2025 crore supports the stated difference within ₹0.0001 crore, whereas CARO prints ₹32.8415 crore with the same difference.

Total March cash ₹43.5869 crore is not all free. The March monitor’s ₹24.96 crore deployment is ring-fenced; audited-result notes show ₹24.31 crore unspent and ₹23.29 crore in FDs, while CARO says ₹39.60 crore idle proceeds in FDs. June object residual ₹20.46 crore versus deployment ₹21.24 crore also requires reconciliation. The base separately assumes ₹3 crore of non-IPO collateral, leaving opening free cash ₹15.6269 crore, and pays gross old tax ₹5.2784 crore once. Government assets ₹14.5602 crore are not assumed liquid or automatically netted against tax. Deposit availability and tax netting are tested. Bank guarantees ₹30.2299 crore and LCs ₹9.6664 crore are contingent, not ordinary funded debt; calls are separate stress cases. Policy recovery and old long-term gratuity are both included at terminal, without double counting.

The combined cash-capex/NWC investment proxy is ₹58.9893 crore versus the financing-side capital increase of ₹68.2297 crore, leaving ₹9.2404 crore unallocated. The basic-NWC subset excludes other advances, government/tax assets and provisions; noncash accruals and comparative reclassifications also affect the bridge. The residual is disclosed rather than falsely attributed. It limits precision, but does not nullify the coherent multi-year capital evidence or prove missing cash.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The verified ₹530.05 quote and 13,967,955 issued shares imply ₹740.3715 crore market value. FY26 PAT implies 52.00× P/E and current-share EPS ₹10.1933; using weighted reported EPS ₹11.35 would understate the current multiple. P/B is 6.64×. Core EBITDA excludes treasury income. Subtracting all March cash gives EV/EBITDA 34.25×; reserving IPO cash and another ₹3 crore collateral raises it to 35.59×. Both mix an October quote with explicitly dated March balances, not an observed October net-debt claim. No separate property value is added to an operating EV already earning profits from those assets.

The cash model integrates a continuously growing annual sales run rate from 31 March 2026 and values the business exactly on 19 October 2031. At 22% run-rate growth, first-year recognized revenue therefore grows less than 22%; this is not a disguised adoption of management’s 20–30% revenue guidance. Bear/base/bull assumptions are growth 8/22/30%, EBITDA margin 8.5/12/15%, operating NWC 32/23/19% of run-rate sales and exit EV/EBITDA 12/18/24×. Maintenance capex continues at 1.5% of sales; recurring growth capex resumes after scheduled initial projects. Lease costs remain within margins. Existing cash-credit debt rolls at 9.5%, remains a terminal claim and is not assumed repaid by gross cash that is restricted.

Actual July funding is ₹11.18 crore, not the full ₹13.76 crore nominal proposed amount. Optional warrant proceeds ₹2.58 crore are zero by default. No automatic new bank draw or rescue is hidden. Each interval tests opening cash, cash immediately before same-day financing receipts, and closing cash. This prevents a late receipt from masking the preceding trough. Monthly/event checkpoints do not establish every unobserved daily bank balance.

The funded conditional base has a minimum modeled free-cash checkpoint of about ₹13.8513 crore, including the July pre-receipt trough. Its IRR is about 12.01%; its 12/15/18% hurdle-equivalent prices are approximately ₹530.29/₹464.65/₹408.52. These are research illustrations only if G2 clears and cash assumptions are verified, not buy levels. Bull conditional IRR is about 33.37%. Bear first breaches the reserve on 31 December 2026; non-rescue return and entry values are therefore null. A separately labeled pre-funded rescue shows whole-share dilution, fees and changed ownership, not available or authorized capital.

Reverse underwriting at a 12% margin, 23% NWC and 18× exit requires about 25.12% annual run-rate growth to earn 15%. At 24× exit the requirement falls to 18.51%, retaining more multiple risk. At 12× no funded crossing exists within 0–80% searched growth; no endpoint is mislabeled as a root. All 58 two-way sensitivity rows are embedded, including NWC/project budgets, growth/multiples, reserves/deposit restrictions, old-tax netting/new debt, contingent calls/optional warrants and continuing capex. All ordinary return and entry outputs remain NS under G2 Hold.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that the order book is fake. It is that low-margin, credit-intensive growth consumes more capital than retained earnings while the market prices a higher-quality compounder. Delayed dispatch raises inventory; dispatch may then move the balance to receivables rather than cash. Concentrated buyers can extend acceptance or retention. Nonexclusive components and fixed-price industrial orders can weaken input-cost recovery. New sites can add depreciation, rent and staff before utilization catches up.

The linked bear case combines 8% growth, 8.5% EBITDA margin, 32% NWC and a 12× exit, rather than stressing each variable in isolation. It breaches the assumed ₹3 crore reserve on 31 December 2026. That is not evidence of an observed default. Reserve sensitivities at ₹0/1/3/5 crore distinguish a discretionary buffer from genuinely negative cash; restricted-deposit sensitivities test the larger uncertainty. Bear non-rescue returns stay null. The separate upfront rescue quantifies dilution and poor economic results without claiming that financing was historically received or is available.

Guarantee calls, unprotected raw-material inflation and impairment of aged receivables are additional permanent-loss routes. Equity issuance can reduce leverage yet dilute owners if incremental returns remain weak. The decisive variable is collected operating profit per incremental rupee of capital. An auditor-backed reconciliation might resolve presentation issues, but until then a seemingly lower multiple alone cannot establish reliable downside value.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold share-price returns over five years require about 37.98% and 58.50% annual returns, far beyond the 15% underwriting hurdle. With unchanged current shares, market values would be ₹3,701.86 crore and ₹7,403.71 crore. At an illustrative 25× terminal P/E, PAT would need ₹148.07 crore or ₹296.15 crore versus FY26 ₹14.24 crore, implying approximately 59.75% or 83.51% annual PAT growth. Future dilution raises the total-profit requirement further.

The ₹471 crore backlog, GIS investment and export opportunity make business expansion plausible, but do not establish those per-share outcomes. Even the bull modeled return is below the annual return required for 5×. Using an extreme terminal multiple to force a 10× result would replace analysis with valuation dependence. These are feasibility constraints, not targets. At the reference price this is not an underwritten 5×/10× case.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Monitoring should close the cash-and-execution loop rather than count order announcements. The highest priority is the next reconciled financial filing: bank returns, restricted cash and aged receivables can change both confidence and the funding model. Shipment, customer acceptance and payment must be checked separately. Given the existing backlog, collected margins and new-asset utilization are more informative than another headline win.

The nine-row register below sets baselines, checks and warning levels. Thresholds are analyst indicators, not asserted bank covenants. G2 resolution could permit ordinary return underwriting. A verified free-cash shortfall, bank nonrenewal or major guarantee call would require prompt G3 reassessment. Before any trade, the dated liquidity analysis needs current restrictions, lot, spread and depth checks. This research does not itself place an order or establish a recurring monitoring service.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved. Resolve financial reliability and cash availability before investment consideration. No BQS, GQS or IAS point ranking is eligible while G2 remains open. Diagnostic BQS 4.92 describes mixed quality, not a demonstrated compounder. Raw GQS 5.70 is capped at 5.0, while IAS is NS. The compounder test independently fails on governance, moat, capital efficiency and cash realization.

A lower share price cannot cure unreliable inputs. If the bank/proceeds issues are resolved and the base cash assumptions validated, approximately ₹465 is a conditional 15% hurdle reference to recalculate with new results, cash and shares, not a standing buy recommendation. At ₹530.05 the funded conditional base return is already below the hurdle. Conversely, verified commissioning, collections and strong incremental returns would justify reassessing the business rather than automatically chasing its price. No portfolio, holding cost, tax position or suitability information was provided, so no personalized allocation or exit-count instruction is inferred.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence includes full FY22–FY26 audits and annexures, the IPO restated accounts, FY26 signed statements and searchable resubmission, March and June monitoring, actual July allotment, October orders, and CARE/CRISIL rationales. Dated NSE security and bhavcopy rows authenticate price, ISIN, series, lot and shares. Source records retain URLs, dates and original-byte hashes where downloaded. CRISIL’s primary HTML was read through the web tool; direct download returned HTTP 406, so its original-byte hash is not claimed. Recalculation from selected source facts does not itself reauthenticate original documents.

Open questions are specific: why bank returns and books diverged; why CARO’s books and idle-proceeds figures conflict with notes; which deposits are pledged, earmarked or free; how monitoring deployment reconciles to object residuals and issue costs; whether aged balances have been confirmed and collected; whether new facilities are fully commissioned; what gratuity expense relates to historical catch-up; and whether funded bank limits remain available. Neither an unanswered question nor a clean headline opinion settles these matters.

Explicit assumptions include a 25.17% cash-tax rate, 9.5% interest, ₹3 crore additional collateral, ₹3 crore free-cash reserve, gross old-tax payment without unverified netting, scheduled remaining projects, no optional warrant balance by default and no automatic rescue or new debt. Conservative policy/collateral recoveries and old gratuity claims are retained at terminal. Sensitivities vary operating and funding requirements jointly. No private statement, acquired revenue, current spread or cutoff surveillance clearance is invented. Source-safe archives contain selected company facts, not raw shareholder lists, personal identifiers or bank-account numbers.

summary:
Hold — unresolved. Parth has a real electrical-equipment business, a credible technical niche and a disclosed ₹471 crore executable order book. New GIS and eastern-India capacity could expand its addressable product and customer base. However, nonexclusive licences and concentrated customers limit the moat; two years of poor cash realization and material bank-return/proceeds inconsistencies prevent ordinary return underwriting.

At ₹530.05 on 19 October 2026, current-share market value is ₹740.37 crore, or 52.00 times FY26 reported PAT. The stipulated, funded base case returns about 12.01% annually versus a 15% hurdle, before resolving the reliability questions. This is a conditional model, not an actionable target. The appropriate research priority is to establish cash availability and reconcile bank submissions, then verify that new orders convert into collected profit and attractive incremental returns. It is not a demonstrated compounder or an underwritten 5× opportunity at this price.
